claim: For the nearest-neighbour cycle Hamiltonian \(H_N=H_0+V(|0\rangle\langle0|+|d\rangle\langle d|)\), with \(N\ge3\), unit hopping, distinct defect sites separated by \(d\in\{1,\ldots,N-1\}\), and equal strengths \(V>0\), there is exactly one eigenvalue above the infinite-chain band \([-2,2]\) for every positive strength, and a second eigenvalue above that band if and only if \(V>2N/[d(N-d)]\); at equality the second branch meets \(E=2\). If \(d_N/N\to\rho\in(0,1/2]\) and \(V_N=\lambda/N\), the second out-of-band eigenvalue appears asymptotically exactly when \(\lambda>2/[\rho(1-\rho)]\). For either existing branch, \(N^2(E_{\pm,N}-2)\to y_\pm^2\), where \(y_\pm>0\) is the unique solution of \(\lambda=\Psi_\pm(y;\rho)\) and \(\Psi_\pm(y;\rho)=\frac{2y\sinh(y/2)}{\cosh(y/2)\pm\cosh((1/2-\rho)y)}\); the minus branch has a positive solution only above the stated threshold.

integrity: The main comparison paper was inspected in full text; the older many-impurity source was available only as an abstract.
Originality is a best-knowledge assessment with explicit residual risk, not an independent novelty certification.
limitations: Equal positive defects only; nearest-neighbour cycle; unit hopping; one-particle Hamiltonian.
At the limiting equality lambda=lambda_c(rho), finite-size count depends on subleading separation corrections.
The numerical checker corroborates formulas but does not prove the infinite family or scaling limit.

title: Two-defect bound-state threshold and separation scaling on a finite cycle
